subject: Dedicated GPU capacity and burst/autoscaling policy for Acme Logistics
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme-logistics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity + burst for peak season

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We liked the Dedicated model and want to get ahead of sizing and contract language. Two questions to start:

1) We run a predictable baseline with short daily peaks (weekday mornings) but also major spikes on shipment holidays and seasonal promos. We need an architecture that guarantees low p99 latency during spikes but also stays cost-effective most of the year.

2) How does Redwood charge for "burst" capacity on Dedicated? Can we lean on an autoscaling policy with pre-warmed GPUs for a limited window, and how is that reconciled with reserved capacity?

Attached is a first-pass summary of our traffic patterns; Samir is cc'd with infra details. Would like a call this week to go over options and get a recommended policy and ballpark costs.

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of Product, Acme Logistics

Attachment: 20250811-acme-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (xlsx, 87KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst for peak season

Jordan,

Great to hear and thanks for the traffic dump. Quick notes before we schedule a walkthrough:

- We typically recommend a baseline reserved pool sized for steady-state 95th percentile concurrency for production traffic. That avoids throttling for normal peaks.
- For holiday spikes, we support two complementary patterns:
  * Pre-warmed burst pool: a small set of GPUs kept ready for immediate use, billed as reserved but contractually tagged as burst capacity with a time-limited usage window.
  * Autoscaling burst: dynamic instances spun up from our fleet as demand grows; these can come from spare Dedicated capacity or cloud burst machines. Billing for autoscaled nodes is charged at the dedicated committed rate plus a transient premium.

I've attached a short template we use to capture baseline RPS, average token lengths, and concurrency targets. If you can fill the highlighted columns Samir mentioned, Rishi and Priya will draft a proposed policy and cost model.

Propose Wed 08/13 10:00 PT for a 45-min sizing call. Does that work?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: see previous

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme-logistics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst for peak season - proposed autoscaling policy

Jordan / Marissa,

Following up with an ops-oriented proposal after looking at the worksheet. High level recommendations and the policy fields we typically surface in the Dedicated contract:

1) Baseline sizing approach
   - Reserve for steady-state 95th percentile concurrency across your normal windows. This minimizes cold starts and keeps p99 predictable.

2) Burst strategy (recommended hybrid)
   - Pre-warmed pool: keep N_prewarm GPUs (configurable) idle/warm for instant acceptance. Good for short, high-impact bursts (few minutes).
   - Autoscale pool: allow dynamic spin-up up to M_burst max instances drawn from our burst fleet. Spin-up time is model + allocation dependent; pre-warmed reduces tail latency.

3) Policy fields (template names we will include in the SOW)
   - min_replicas: minimum GPUs kept for baseline (e.g., 8)
   - max_replicas: upper safety bound for autoscale (e.g., baseline + 40)
   - prewarm_count: GPUs pre-warmed and immediately available (e.g., 4)
   - max_burst_minutes: maximum contiguous time autoscale may use burst capacity without manual approval (e.g., 120 minutes)
   - cooldown_window: cooldown after a burst before scale-down starts (e.g., 10 minutes)
   - scale_step: number of GPUs to add per scale event to avoid thundering herd (e.g., 2)
   - priority_policy: routing preference (baseline pool first, then prewarm, then autoscale)
   - fallback_model: automatic downgrade to a smaller, cheaper model when burst > threshold to preserve availability

4) Billing model options
   - Option A (preferred for predictability): baseline billed as reserved monthly. Pre-warmed GPUs billed into baseline for contract term but with a capped usage allowance for burst-tagged hours. Autoscale billed at committed rate + 25-35% transient premium.
   - Option B (flexible): baseline reserved, pre-warm charged as reserved for a partial commit, autoscale billed purely on usage but subject to spot availability for the lowest-cost pools.

5) SLAs and fallbacks
   - For guaranteed p99 latency during holidays we recommend increasing prewarm_count and setting fallback_model to ensure graceful degradation rather than outright rejects.

6) Operational controls
   - Canary window for new policies, automatic rollback on latency/regression metrics, enhanced tracing hooks.

If you can confirm key numbers for baseline RPS, avg tokens per request, and your acceptable billing approach, we will crank out a draft SOW with the above fields populated. Happy to go into the math on GPU throughput if useful on the call.

- Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme-logistics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-logistics.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst for peak season - numbers

Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks — the worksheet is populated (columns for baseline 95th, avg tokens, and expected holiday multipliers). Key points from infra:
- Baseline concurrency: 120 concurrent sessions (chat-style workloads)
- Average request tokens: 250 tokens inbound + 200 tokens model output
- Expected holiday multiplier: 6x sustained for spikes up to 4 hours, with short micro-peaks up to 10x for 10-20 minutes

Two questions from finance/procurement:
1) If we use Option A, how do you meter burst hours across the contract months? Is there a monthly cap before overage pricing kicks in?
2) For autoscale spin-up, what is the realistic warm-start time for our model family if we do not pre-warm? We want to avoid user-facing timeouts.

Samir - I looped you to confirm if Acme can accept a small pre-warm commitment for the holiday window.

Best,
Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst for peak season - SOW next steps

Jordan,

Appreciate the detailed numbers — that's exactly what we need. Summary and next steps:

Summary of recommended policy (SOW draft will include exact numbers and a table):
- Baseline: reserve for 95th concurrency = 120 sessions mapped to min_replicas.
- Pre-warm pool: recommend prewarm_count = 8 GPUs during holiday windows (2x safety factor for micro-peaks).
- Autoscale: max_burst up to +400% of baseline for emergency use with max_burst_minutes = 240 before an operational review.
- Cooldown: 15 minutes for graceful scale-down to avoid oscillation.
- Billing: Option A with a rolling monthly burst allowance of 150 hours per month at the committed premium. Overage beyond 150 hrs billed at transient premium rate. We will add a clause to permit accrual of unused burst hours into a small buffer for the holiday month only.
- SLA: guaranteed p99 latency targets during approved holiday windows when pre-warm is in effect; outside approved windows, autoscale best-effort with a transient premium.

Next steps:
1) Rishi to produce the SOW policy table populated with your numbers and a cost model by EOD Monday.
2) We will add the pre-warm credit language and a DocuSign SOW link for signature.
3) Kickoff deployment plan with Redwood Private/Dedicated infra team and a 2-week canary prior to your first holiday window.

If that aligns, I'll put together the SOW and send the DocuSign link. Please confirm acceptance of the monthly 150 burst-hour allowance and the proposed cooldown.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
